MTX-061.transaction_boundary: Catalog validation is a read-only precondition committing nothing. Snapshot seal: one transaction creating the single immutable Check Applicability Snapshot with its content hash, after which no expected entry may be added, removed or reordered. Key materialization: one transaction per preimage that atomically creates or returns one Check Result identity BEFORE execution. Execution: the attempt runs outside any transaction and only its semantic output is committed onto the materialized identity, in expected-key order. No external call sits inside a database transaction, because no Check makes an external call at all.
MTX-061.concurrency: Materialization atomically creates or returns one Check Result identity per retained preimage before execution, so two concurrent executors cannot produce two Results for one key. Concurrent completion is committed in expected-key order. Exact or concurrent replay with the same deterministic input returns that identity and its terminal semantic output and emits no second `CheckResultCreated`. Because the Snapshot is sealed before any execution, completion order never changes the expected-entry set, its order or its content hash. At exactly five elapsed seconds `check_internal_timeout` wins the race against completion; a later completion is discarded and cannot create or replace a Check Result.
MTX-061.idempotency: The retained canonical uniqueness preimage -- Evaluation ID, Evaluation Input Snapshot ID, Check Applicability Snapshot ID, Check Catalog version, Check Definition ID and version, canonical subject type and key, and pillar ID in that order -- is uniqueness authority within the Evaluation; `check_result_key_sha256` is its canonical-JSON SHA-256 and is an index, never the authority. Exact replay returns the stored identity and terminal semantic output. A DIFFERENT deterministic input for the same preimage fails the Evaluation as `F1-DATA-409 / check_result_input_conflict` and changes neither Result. A same hash with a different retained preimage never merges: it creates distinct internal collision records, emits restricted `CheckResultFingerprintCollision` telemetry, and fails the affected Evaluation as `check_result_key_collision` before Check execution. Altered input under the same result identity is `idempotency_conflict` and fails the Evaluation.
MTX-061.background_job: `CheckExecutionWorker` per materialized expected key, and `CheckRetryTimer` for the single permitted retry exactly one second after a retryable attempt terminalizes. The five-second attempt ceiling is enforced inside the attempt, not by a separate job.
MTX-061.queue: The evaluation queue, per the Volume I Background Processing action registry. Queue identity and worker topology are owned by BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md; this row does not rename them.
MTX-061.retry_policy: `check-executor-interim-v1` exactly: each attempt has five elapsed seconds and at exactly five seconds `check_internal_timeout` wins over completion. Only `check_dependency_unavailable` and `check_internal_timeout` are retryable, receiving one initial attempt and exactly one retry starting one second after the failed attempt completes, reusing the identical applicability entry, Evidence tuple, input hash and attempt identity lineage. No other reason retries. Passed, failed and not-applicable results use one attempt. This bounded per-result retry is the ONLY retry inside an Evaluation.
MTX-061.terminal_failure: Retry exhaustion persists one `error` Check Result with outcome and `error_reason_code` both equal to `check_dependency_unavailable` or `check_internal_timeout`, `execution_attempt_count=2`, null `confidence_value`, `confidence_status=missing`, display band `low`, null `impact_band`, no Issue, and `subject_set_complete=false`. A semantic input problem persists a one-attempt `error`. Handled `error` Results are terminal and do NOT fail WF-007; after every expected entry is terminal the Evaluation may complete, the affected pillar is insufficient and the overall score becomes unavailable. Catalog, Definition, applicability-snapshot, tenant-integrity or result-idempotency failure instead transitions the Evaluation to failed and publishes no Issue Set.
MTX-061.reconciliation: Each expected entry ultimately yields exactly one Check Result or the whole Evaluation fails under the Catalog, applicability and integrity boundary; there is no third outcome and no expected entry is silently omitted. A missing selected input permitted by an otherwise valid selector remains an entry and produces the Definition's handled `error`. A retry or replay whose computed output differs for the same deterministic input fails as `check_nondeterministic_output`, publishes no replacement Result or Issue, and preserves the original attempt evidence for restricted diagnosis.
